# ZeroClaw — Native Operator Console

Native Rust GUI built on `eframe`/`egui`. Mirrors the layout, navigation, and theme of the web operator console while talking directly to the ZeroClaw core over **tonic + tonic-web** with **server reflection**.

## Run

```bash
cargo run --release
# point at a remote core:
ZEROCLAW_GRPC=https://op.local:443 cargo run --release
```

## Architecture

```text
.zeroclaw/
├── Cargo.toml
└── src/
    ├── main.rs        # eframe entry + background tokio runtime
    ├── app.rs         # topbar + sidebar + routed shell
    ├── nav.rs         # NAV_GROUPS port (1:1 mirror of React nav)
    ├── theme.rs       # graphite/slate dark theme tokens
    ├── grpc.rs        # tonic-web client + ServerReflection bootstrap
    ├── schema.rs      # schemars Schema → egui renderer (schema-as-code)
    └── views/mod.rs   # per-route views (Inspector/State/gRPC are schema-driven)
```

## gRPC + reflection

`grpc.rs` opens a `tonic::transport::Channel` (works for both native gRPC and
`tonic-web` proxied endpoints), calls `ServerReflectionClient::server_reflection_info`,
and loads every returned `FileDescriptorProto` into a `prost_reflect::DescriptorPool`.

From the pool we can:

- enumerate services + methods (rendered in the **gRPC Diagnostics** view)
- decode any response payload into `serde_json::Value` via `DynamicMessage`
  (`grpc::decode_to_json`)

Server side (in `op-web`) needs:

```rust
let reflection = tonic_reflection::server::Builder::configure()
    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(zeroclaw_proto::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(tonic_health::pb::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
    .build_v1()?;

Server::builder()
    .accept_http1(true)
    .layer(tonic_web::GrpcWebLayer::new())
    .add_service(reflection)
    .add_service(/* your services */)
    .serve(addr).await?;
```

## Schema-as-code

Plugins in `crates/op-plugins` already derive `schemars::JsonSchema` on their
state structs (`schemars = "1"`). Emit a schema with:

```rust
let schema = schemars::schema_for!(MyPluginState);
```

Ship that schema alongside the decoded JSON (from `grpc::decode_to_json`) and
call `schema::render_value(ui, &schema, &value)` — the GUI renders titles,
descriptions, required fields, enums, nested objects, and arrays with no
hand-written form code. See `views::inspector` / `views::state_view` for a live
demo using a `DemoPluginState` struct that mirrors the plugin contract.

## Adding a real plugin

1. In `op-plugins`, derive `#[derive(JsonSchema)]` on the state struct.
2. In `op-web`, return `(message_bytes, schemars::schema_for!(State))` on the
   relevant gRPC stream (or expose the schema via a sibling `GetSchema` RPC).
3. In this crate, decode with `grpc::decode_to_json` and render with
   `schema::render_value` — no per-plugin UI code required.

**What I did:**
1. Read `lovable/.zeroclaw/README.md` first — confirmed it's a native `eframe`/`egui` GUI that mirrors the web console and talks to the core over tonic + tonic-web with server reflection.

**Run it:**
```bash
zeroclaw-gui
# point at a remote core:
ZEROCLAW_GRPC=https://op.local:443 zeroclaw-gui
```

Note: it's a GUI app, so it needs a display (X11/Wayland) — launching it from this headless session would fail at the eframe window-creation step. The default gRPC endpoint baked into `main.rs` is `http://assistant.3tched.com:50051`; override with `ZEROCLAW_GRPC` to hit a different core.

One thing worth flagging: `grpc::decode_to_json` and a few other functions are compiled-but-unused (the dead-code warnings) — meaning the schema-driven decode path the README advertises is wired but not yet called from the live views. #!/bin/sh
# zeroclaw-gui-srv: native ZeroClaw operator console (eframe/egui) on its own
# dedicated headless Xvfb display. No CRD, no XFCE — a private virtual X11
# server with software GL, torn down with the app via xvfb-run.
set -eu
exec 2>&1

user=jeremy
uid=1000
home_dir=/home/jeremy
runtime_dir="/run/user/$uid"

export HOME="$home_dir"
export USER="$user"
export LOGNAME="$user"
export SHELL=/bin/bash
export PATH="$home_dir/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$runtime_dir"
export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
# ZeroClaw core gRPC endpoint (matches the binary's built-in default; override here).
export ZEROCLAW_GRPC="http://assistant.3tched.com:50051"

install -d -m 0700 -o "$user" -g "$user" "$runtime_dir"

cd "$home_dir"
# xvfb-run -a: auto-pick a free display so a stale lock after an unclean
# restart never blocks startup. Xvfb dies when zeroclaw-gui exits.
exec s6-setuidgid "$user" \
    xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x800x24 -nolisten tcp" \
    "$home_dir/.local/bin/zeroclaw-gui"

name: project_s6_commit_prune_hazard
description: s6-frontend `s6 set commit` prunes the live-referenced compiled db, dangling bootdb; safe recovery procedure
metadata:

---

On this Artix box, `s6 set commit` (s6-frontend) compiles a new db AND garbage-collects the old compiled db **even though `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` (the `bootdb` per `s6-frontend.conf`) still hardlinks it by full path**. If `s6 live install` doesn't immediately follow (e.g. it fails on a lock), you're left with: dangling `bootdb` (reboot can fail), and `/run/s6-rc/state` keyed to the now-gone db so `s6-rc` reports "unable to read valid state". Running services are UNAFFECTED — s6-svscan supervises them independently; only the s6-rc management/boot layer breaks.

**Always do `s6 set commit` and `s6 live install` back-to-back.** The window between them is the hazard.

**Recovery when the old db is already pruned (validated, no service disruption):**
1. Preserve the new db to a stable path outside `/etc/s6/repo/compiled` gc scope: `cp -a <repo/compiled/current> /etc/s6/manualdb/<name>`.
2. Reconstruct an old-equiv db: `s6 set mask <newsvcs>` (NOT `disable` — disable keeps them in the db; only `mask` removes from db) → `s6 set commit`. Deterministic compile reproduces the lost db's numbering.
3. Point `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` -> old-equiv. READ-ONLY VALIDATE: `s6-rc -a list` must read state AND up/down must match ground truth (`s6-svstat` each `/run/s6-rc/servicedirs/*`). Mismatch → abort.
4. Dry-run `s6-rc-update -n -v2 -l /run/s6-rc <preserved-new-db>` — confirm stop-list and start-list are EMPTY (no disruption), then run for real.
5. Point `bootdb` -> preserved new db. Reconcile frontend: `s6 set unmask` + `s6 set enable` + `s6 set commit`.

Keeping boot/live on the stable `/etc/s6/manualdb` copy (not `repo/compiled/current`) makes it immune to future commit gc. See [[artix-s6-layout]]. New service installed this way: zeroclaw-gui-srv/-log (see [[project_zeroclaw_gui_service]]).

#!/bin/sh
# s6-apply — the ONE safe way to push s6-frontend working-set changes live.
#
# Why this exists: `s6 set commit` compiles a new db AND garbage-collects the
# old one. If `s6 live install` does not immediately follow, the live-referenced
# compiled db can vanish, dangling the bootdb and breaking /run/s6-rc state
# (services keep running, but s6-rc management + next boot break). This wrapper
# performs sync -> commit -> live install back-to-back, keeps the bootdb in sync
# with the live db, and on any failure restores the bootdb so boot stays safe.
#
# Run this instead of `s6 set commit` / `s6 live install` by hand.
set -eu

log()  { printf '[s6-apply] %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { log "FATAL: $*"; exit 1; }

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || die "must run as root (try: sudo s6-apply)"

bootdb=/etc/s6/rc/compiled

# Remember the db the live system is currently on, so we can keep boot safe
# if the transition fails partway.
live_before=$(readlink -f /run/s6-rc/compiled 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -n "$live_before" ] && [ -d "$live_before" ] \
    || die "cannot resolve current live db (/run/s6-rc/compiled); refusing to proceed"
log "current live db: $live_before"

# 1. Pull any new/removed service defs from the stores into the working set.
log "syncing repository with stores"
s6 repository sync || die "repository sync failed (nothing changed)"

# 2. Compile the working set. After this point the old repo db may be pruned,
#    so step 3 MUST run — that is the whole reason for this wrapper.
log "committing working set"
s6 set commit || die "commit failed (nothing installed; live db untouched)"

# 3. Transition the live system onto the committed set.
if ! s6 live install -b; then
    log "live install failed — restoring bootdb to keep boot safe"
    ln -sfn "$live_before" "$bootdb"
    die "live install failed; live db left on $live_before. Investigate before retrying."
fi

# 4. Keep the bootdb pointed at exactly what the live system now runs, so the
#    next boot matches the running set.
live_after=$(readlink -f /run/s6-rc/compiled)
ln -sfn "$live_after" "$bootdb"

# 5. Sanity: s6-rc must be able to read live state against the new db.
s6-rc -a list >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "post-install s6-rc state read failed — DO NOT REBOOT, investigate"

log "ok. live + bootdb -> $live_after"
